text:
BUILDING MANAGEMENT NOTICE: Monthly Fire Alarm Test

All tenants are reminded that the fire alarm system will be tested on the first Monday of every month at 10 a.m. The test will last approximately ten minutes, during which the alarm will sound continuously. Tenants are not required to leave the building, [1] they should not assume that the alarm indicates a test unless an announcement is made to that effect.

If an alarm sounds at any other time, it must be treated as genuine, and everyone should proceed immediately to the nearest exit. [2] Lifts will be taken [3] service during an evacuation, so the stairwells should be used at all times. Anyone who needs assistance to leave the building should register with the front desk, so that arrangements can be [4] in advance.

The next test will take place on Monday 6 October. Further guidance is available in section 7 of the Tenant Handbook.

questions.explanation: 'Even though tenants are not required to leave, they should not assume ...' concedes a fact before a warning. 'Inasmuch as' and 'so long as' give a reason or a condition that makes no sense here, and 'in case' expresses a precaution.

choices: Tenants should not stop to collect personal belongings, and should wait at their desks for instructions from the front desk.
Tenants should not stop to collect personal belongings, and should report to the assembly point once the alarm has been silenced.
Tenants should not stop to collect personal belongings, and should close doors behind them without locking them.
Tenants should stop to collect personal belongings, and should lock doors behind them before leaving the floor.
questions.explanation: The previous sentence orders everyone to 'proceed immediately to the nearest exit', so only an instruction that keeps people moving fits: no stopping for belongings and closing doors without locking them. Stopping to collect items, waiting at desks for instructions, or reporting to the assembly point only once the alarm is silenced all contradict 'immediately'.
'Taken out of service' is the fixed expression meaning no longer operating; 'off', 'away from' and 'beyond' do not combine with 'service' in this way.
'Arrangements can be made' is the standard collocation; 'arrangements' are not 'taken', 'given' or 'held'.

text:
To: Warehouse Managers
From: Ludovica Ferrante, Supply Chain Director
Subject: Peak-season staffing

As in previous years, demand will peak between mid-November and the end of December, and I should like to confirm the arrangements for temporary staff. [1] In response, agencies have been asked to supply workers who can start at short notice and who have completed the mandatory safety induction.

Managers are [2] for estimating their requirements by shift and for submitting them to me by 30 September. [3] the cost of temporary labor has risen, the alternative of understaffing would be far more expensive, since late deliveries incur penalties under most of our contracts. [4] requests received after the deadline, we cannot guarantee that agencies will be able to supply the numbers required. A provisional budget of £210,000 has been allocated across the five sites and will be adjusted once the forecasts have been reviewed.

choices: Last year, a shortage of storage space in mid-December delayed more than forty customer shipments.
In earlier years, a fall in customer orders in mid-December left many temporary staff without work.
Last year, a surplus of trained staff in mid-December raised labor costs well above the planned budget.
Last year, a shortage of trained staff in mid-December delayed more than forty customer shipments.
questions.explanation: 'In response' in the next sentence needs a problem that agencies supplying workers at short notice would solve, namely a staffing shortage. A surplus of staff, a lack of storage space and a drop in orders would not be answered by workers who can start immediately.

Managers are 'responsible for' estimating requirements, the fixed adjective plus preposition. 'Responsive' means quick to react, 'respondent' is a noun, and 'responsibly' is an adverb that cannot follow 'are'.

'Although the cost of temporary labor has risen' concedes a drawback before the main argument that understaffing would cost more. 'Unless' sets a condition, and 'given that' and 'now that' would present the rise in cost as the reason for the conclusion.

'In the case of requests received after the deadline' introduces the specific situation to which the warning applies. 'In lieu of' means instead of, 'in pursuit of' means chasing, and 'in excess of' means more than.

text:
Hotel Review: The Alder House, Edinburgh
Rating: 4 out of 5 stars

The Alder House occupies a restored Georgian townhouse five minutes' walk from the castle. [1] Our room, which overlooked a quiet square, combined period features such as high ceilings and sash windows with a modern bathroom and an excellent bed.

Staff were attentive without being intrusive, and breakfast, which uses produce from local suppliers, was consistently good. We also dined in the hotel restaurant on the second evening, and the seasonal menu was both imaginative and well presented. [2], prices are high: a double room costs almost double the city average, at £240 per night against roughly £125, and the lack of a lift may be [3] for guests with limited mobility. [4] these drawbacks, I would stay again without hesitation.

Stayed: March, two nights, as part of a leisure trip.

choices: The conversion has been done with evident care, and the character of the original building has largely been preserved.
The conversion has been carried out with evident haste, and the character of the original building has largely been lost.
The conversion has been carried out with evident care, but the character of the original rooms has largely been lost.
The conversion will be carried out with evident care, and the character of the original building will largely be preserved.
questions.explanation: The next sentence describes a room that keeps 'high ceilings and sash windows' alongside modern comforts, so the preceding sentence must say the original character was preserved. 'Haste' and a loss of character contradict those period features, and the future tense clashes with 'restored' and with a review of a past stay.

'Admittedly' concedes a weakness after praise and prepares the negative point 'prices are high'. 'Similarly' adds a parallel point, 'subsequently' marks time order, and 'accordingly' signals a result, none of which fits a concession.

The lack of a lift may be 'problematic' for guests with limited mobility, which is a drawback. 'Prosperous' and 'profitable' describe wealth and gain, and 'persistent' describes something that continues, so none of them fits the reviewer's complaint.

'Despite these drawbacks' concedes the faults and leads to the surprising conclusion 'I would stay again'. 'Besides' adds to them, 'given' would imply that the faults justify not returning, and 'following' only marks sequence.

text:
Dear Professor Linden,

On behalf of the programme committee, I am delighted to invite you to give a plenary lecture at the International Symposium on Sustainable Materials, to be held in Lisbon from 8 to 10 September. [1] In particular, your recent paper on biodegradable composites generated considerable discussion among committee members, and we believe that it would be of great interest to delegates.

The symposium will cover the cost of your accommodation for three nights and will [2] your airfare up to a maximum of €800. We should be grateful if you could let us know by 15 April whether you are able to accept, [3] your name can be included in the preliminary program. If you wish to be [4] by a coauthor or a student, please inform us, and we shall endeavor to arrange a reduced registration fee. The lecture will last forty-five minutes, followed by fifteen minutes for questions.

Yours sincerely,
Beatriz Calado

choices: Your research on sustainable materials has attracted considerable attention within the committee over the past two years.
Your research on sustainable materials has attracted considerable attention within the committee, though its relevance to delegates is unclear.
Our symposium on sustainable materials has attracted considerable attention within the sector over the past two years.
Your research on sustainable materials has attracted considerable criticism within the committee over the past two years.
questions.explanation: 'In particular, your recent paper' must narrow down a general positive statement about the professor's own research and the committee's interest. Mentioning 'criticism', doubting relevance to delegates, or talking about the symposium instead of the professor's research fails to lead into 'we believe that it would be of great interest to delegates'.

The symposium will 'reimburse' the airfare, meaning repay the cost up to €800. 'Reinstate' and 'redeem' do not take an airfare as their object in this sense, and 'reclaim' would mean the professor recovers it rather than the symposium paying.
'So that your name can be included' gives the purpose of asking for a reply by 15 April. 'Even if', 'in case' and 'whereas' do not express purpose and would make the deadline illogical.
After 'to be' the passive requires a past participle: 'to be accompanied by a coauthor or a student'. 'Accompanying', 'accompany' and 'accompanies' cannot follow 'to be' in this passive.

text:
Smaller Firms Embrace Four-Day Trials

A growing number of small businesses are experimenting with a four-day working week, [1] fears that productivity will suffer. Among them is Calderwood Print, a firm of thirty employees in Leeds, which reduced its week to thirty-two hours last spring without a cut in pay. [2] Its managing director, Laura Voss, attributes the improvement to better morale, noting that output has held steady while absenteeism has fallen by a quarter. A pilot scheme covering sixty-one companies found similar patterns, with revenue broadly unchanged after six months.

Critics, [3], doubt that the model can be applied across the economy. Roles that require constant availability, such as those in customer support, are difficult to cover without additional staff. Ms. Voss [4] that the model may not suit every sector, but says that the experiment has been worthwhile for her own company.

questions.explanation: 'Despite fears that productivity will suffer' expresses concession: firms are trying the scheme although they fear a loss. 'Owing to', 'due to' and 'thanks to' express cause, which would wrongly make the fears the reason for the trials.

choices: The trial, which runs until September, will exceed the expectations of the company's management if output holds steady.
The trial, which runs until September, has so far greatly exceeded the expectations of the company's management.
The trial, which runs until September, has so far fallen short of the expectations of the company's management.
The trial, which runs until September, has so far cost more than the company's management had originally budgeted.
questions.explanation: The next sentence refers to 'the improvement' and reports steady output and lower absenteeism, so the preceding sentence must announce favorable results. Results that 'fell short of expectations' and a trial that 'cost more' than budgeted describe no improvement, and a conditional 'will exceed ... if output holds steady' contradicts the report that output has already held steady.

The critics' doubt contrasts with the encouraging results just described, and 'however' marks that contrast. 'Consequently', 'likewise' and 'accordingly' would present the doubt as a result or a similarity.

'Acknowledges that the model may not suit every sector, but says ...' fits because the 'but' introduces what she maintains despite the concession. 'Denies' and 'insists' contradict the cautious 'may not suit', and 'pretends' implies insincerity.

text:
To: Training Participants
From: Cordelia Marsh, Learning Coordinator
Subject: Postponement of the leadership workshop

I regret to inform you that the leadership workshop scheduled for 12 and 13 May has had to be postponed, owing to the unexpected illness of the facilitator. The new dates are 9 and 10 June, and the venue will remain unchanged. [1] Those who are unable to attend on the revised dates should inform me by 20 May so that a place can be reserved for them in the next available session.

In the meantime, I would ask you to [2] the pre-workshop questionnaire, [3] the original deadline of 5 May has passed. Responses that have already been submitted will be retained, and no further action is required on your part. Travel and accommodation bookings made through the training office will be amended free of charge. [4] you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me.

choices: All participants who attended the previous session were transferred automatically to the revised dates without reapplying.
All participants currently registered will be removed automatically from the revised dates unless they reapply in writing.
All participants currently registered must confirm in writing that they can attend the revised dates by 5 May.
All participants currently registered will be transferred automatically to the revised dates without having to reapply.
questions.explanation: The sentence that follows deals with 'those who are unable to attend', which presupposes that everyone else keeps a place, and a later sentence says 'no further action is required'. Automatic transfer 'without having to reapply' fits both. A duty to reapply or confirm contradicts 'no further action', and the past-tense statement about a previous session does not apply to this workshop.

Participants are asked to 'complete the pre-workshop questionnaire', meaning fill it in. 'Compile' and 'compose' mean assemble or write, and 'comprise' means consist of, so none of them suits a form that already exists.

'Even though the original deadline of 5 May has passed' concedes that the date is gone yet the task is still requested. 'As though' makes a comparison, and 'so that' and 'such that' express purpose or result, neither of which fits.

'Should you have any questions' is an inverted conditional meaning 'if you have any questions', the standard closing of a formal email. 'Albeit', 'insofar' and 'whereas' cannot open a conditional clause.

text:
Greystone Apartments – Maintenance Requests

Residents who wish to report a fault should do so through the online portal, which is monitored daily. Requests are classified as urgent, routine or cosmetic, and the target time for a response depends on the category: twenty-four hours for urgent faults, five working days for routine faults, and thirty days for cosmetic repairs. [1]

Where a fault is [2] by a resident, for example through misuse or negligence, the cost of repair may be charged to the tenant. Access to the apartment will normally be arranged in advance [3] in an emergency, when staff may enter without notice. Repairs are carried out between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., [4] a different time has been agreed. For emergencies outside office hours, residents should telephone the 24-hour line on 0161 555 0142 rather than use the portal.

choices: A resident who has not received a response within these periods may escalate the matter to the property manager.
A resident who has not received a response within these periods will be charged for the repair by the property manager.
A property manager who has not received a request within these periods may escalate the matter to the resident.
A resident who had not received a response within those periods could escalate the matter to the property manager.
questions.explanation: 'These periods' refers to the target response times, so the sentence must say what a resident can do when a deadline is missed: escalate to the property manager. A past-tense version does not describe the current procedure, reversing the roles makes the manager the complainant, and charging a resident for a late response contradicts the rule that charges apply to faults the resident caused.

A fault 'caused by a resident, for example through misuse or negligence' is one the resident brought about, which justifies charging the repair; 'concealed', 'contested' and 'corrected' do not fit 'through misuse or negligence'.

'Except in an emergency' states the one exception to advance arrangement of access; 'besides' means in addition to, 'whereas' contrasts two clauses and 'albeit' concedes, and neither can be followed by 'in an emergency' here.

'Unless a different time has been agreed' states the condition under which the 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. rule does not apply; 'whilst', 'whenever' and 'provided' would either contrast or make the standard hours dependent on a different time being agreed.

text:
To: Finance Staff
From: Arvid Nilsson, Financial Controller
Subject: Year-end closing procedures

The financial year will close on 31 December, and the following procedures apply to all departments. All invoices received by 15 December must be approved and entered into the system by 22 December. [1] Invoices that arrive after 15 December will be recorded as accruals, which will be reversed in January once the actual amounts are confirmed.

Departments are asked to [2] their outstanding commitments by 18 December, so that the accruals can be estimated with reasonable accuracy. [3] a department fails to do so, the controller's office will make its own estimate, which may differ significantly from the final figure. The external auditors will arrive on 12 January, and they will expect all supporting documents to be [4] by that date.

Expense claims for the current year must reach the finance office by 20 December; claims received later will be charged to next year's budget.

choices: This left one week for queries to be resolved before the ledgers were locked at the close of business on 29 December.
This leaves one week for queries to be resolved before the ledgers are locked at the close of business on 19 December.
This leaves one week for queries to be resolved before the ledgers are locked at the close of business on 29 December.
This leaves one week for queries to be resolved before the ledgers are locked at the close of business on 5 January.
questions.explanation: Invoices must be approved by 22 December, so a lock date of 29 December really does leave 'one week'. A lock on 5 January would leave two weeks, a lock on 19 December would fall before the approval deadline, and 'left' and 'were locked' use the past tense for a future procedure.
Departments must 'confirm' (verify) their outstanding commitments so that the accruals can be estimated. 'Confide' means to share secrets, 'confine' means to restrict, and 'conform' means to comply.

'Where a department fails to do so' introduces the specific case in which the controller makes an estimate. 'Whereas' would contrast two facts, and 'wherein' and 'whereby' cannot open a conditional case.
'To be available by that date' needs the adjective 'available'. 'Availed', 'availing' and 'avail' are verb forms that do not give a meaningful passive or complement after 'be'.

text:
NOTICE TO TENANTS

The building management will replace the main water supply pipes on the second and third floors between 3 and 7 March. [1] The latter option, which involves a short interruption on each floor in turn, was chosen because it keeps the rest of the building fully operational.

Water will be suspended on each floor between 9 a.m. and 1 p.m. on the day of the work, and tenants are asked to [2] any items stored beneath sinks so that the contractors can gain access. [3] the work extend beyond 7 March, the management has arranged a temporary supply from the ground-floor kitchen. Any damage caused by the contractors will be repaired at no cost to tenants, [4] it is reported to the office within seven days. Questions may be addressed to the building manager, Ms. Delgado, on extension 214.

choices: Two schedules were considered: replacing all of the pipes simultaneously, or proceeding floor by floor.
The pipes will be replaced floor by floor; the alternative would have been to replace them all simultaneously.
Two schedules were considered: replacing all of the pipes simultaneously, or closing the building for a week.
Two schedules were considered: proceeding floor by floor, or replacing all of the pipes simultaneously.
questions.explanation: 'The latter option' refers to the second of two alternatives, and it must be the work done floor by floor 'in turn'. Only the sentence ending with 'or proceeding floor by floor' fits; the reordered version and the 'alternative' version make the latter option the simultaneous replacement, and closing the building would not match the short interruption on each floor.
Tenants are asked to 'clear' items from beneath sinks so that the contractors can gain access. 'Clean', 'clarify' and 'claim' do not achieve that purpose.

'Should the work extend beyond 7 March' is an inverted conditional meaning 'if the work extends', and the base form 'extend' matches it. 'Had' would require a past participle, 'whether' needs an alternative and 'unless' reverses the logic of a back-up arrangement.
'Provided that it is reported' means on condition that it is reported, and it is a fixed conjunction. 'Provided on', 'provide that' and 'provision that' are not valid conjunctions in this position.

text:
Retail analysts expect consumer spending to remain subdued through the first half of next year. [1] The former is expected to ease gradually as supply chains recover, whereas the latter is likely to persist until central banks begin to reduce interest rates. A survey of 1,200 shoppers by Calloway Research found that 41 percent intend to cut discretionary spending.

Retailers are therefore expected to [2] a cautious approach to stocking and promotions. Large chains are likely to cope reasonably well, [3] smaller independent stores will struggle to absorb higher costs without raising prices. Online retailers, which now account for nearly a third of sales, are expected to fare slightly better. Analysts advise investors not to read too much [4] a single quarter's figures, since seasonal patterns can distort short-term trends and mask the underlying direction of demand.

choices: Two pressures are widely cited: a sharp increase in the cost of borrowing and elevated input costs.
Several pressures are widely cited, including elevated input costs, weak wage growth and the cost of borrowing.
Two pressures are widely cited: elevated input costs and a sharp increase in the cost of borrowing.
Two pressures are widely cited: weak wage growth and a sharp increase in the cost of borrowing.
questions.explanation: 'The former' must be the pressure that eases as supply chains recover (input costs) and 'the latter' the one lasting until rates fall (borrowing), so the sentence must list exactly two items in that order. Listing borrowing first reverses them, 'weak wage growth' would not ease with supply chains, and a list of three items cannot be split into former and latter.

'Adopt a cautious approach' follows from subdued spending, as the word 'therefore' signals. 'Abandon', 'resist' and 'replace' would mean retailers move away from caution, which contradicts the forecast.
'Whereas' contrasts large chains that cope well with smaller stores that will struggle. 'Whereby' and 'wherein' are relative adverbs, and 'whenever' expresses time rather than contrast.
'Read too much into' is the fixed idiom for over-interpreting something, here 'a single quarter's figures'. 'Onto', 'upon' and 'over' do not combine with 'read too much' in this sense.
